answer.A: Increase the daily classroom learning time to 10 hours and reduce students' outdoor activity time to concentrate on learning and reduce the risk of myopia.

The outdoor sports duration is relatively longer in the lower - age group but still insufficient. By designing interesting outdoor activities, primary school students can be attracted to participate, and their relatively good sports foundation can be used to prevent the deterioration of myopia.
answer.C: Focus on increasing the outdoor activity time of senior students. The outdoor sports duration is significantly shorter among senior students, and the data on the number of myopic students shows that the myopia rate in the middle - school and high - school student groups remains relatively high. By prioritizing the arrangement of outdoor courses for senior students, the myopia risk of this group can be alleviated in a targeted manner, and the overall intervention efficiency can be improved.
answer.D: Since the outdoor sports duration of children aged 6 - 9 is the longest (64.3 minutes), which is close to the minimum standard of 120 minutes, there is no need to increase the promotion of outdoor activities for this age group.

answer.F: Integrate eye - health screening and functions expected by parents into the school health plan. Parents have prominent demands for quickly understanding the eye - health status and early - warning functions. Combined with the fact that most people rely on doctors' advice when not getting glasses immediately, schools can introduce portable screening tools to provide instant analysis and suggestions, so as to reduce the delay in intervention.
answer.G: Promote the use of high - brightness electronic teaching equipment, such as tablets, to improve classroom lighting and vision protection.
